case_title: KASHIBAI & ORS. v. THE STATE OF KARNATAKA
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.498A and s.306, sentenced to imprisonment and fine
neutral_facts: The deceased, a woman, married one of the accused approximately three years prior to the incident. The accused, who were the deceased's in-laws, were alleged to have subjected her to physical and mental harassment due to dowry demands. The deceased was found dead in a well, and the prosecution alleged that the accused had harassed her to the point of suicide. The prosecution relied on the testimony of the deceased's parents and uncle, as well as a neighbor, to establish the harassment. However, the evidence did not conclusively show that the accused had instigated or aided the deceased in committing suicide. The post-mortem report indicated the cause of death was drowning due to asphyxia, but there was no evidence to determine whether the death was accidental or suicidal. The prosecution failed to establish that the accused had abetted the deceased's suicide, despite the harassment allegations.
